title: Ovara policy document (contract C2, spec 0.1)
description: A policy is a JSON document with a version, a precedence, a default decision and a list of rules. It is what runtime/gateway/internal/policy loads; see spec/policy.md for how rules are matched and how overlapping rules resolve.

version.description: An operator's label for this policy; it goes into every receipt as part of the policy hash. Empty means the loader's hint, else "v1-default".

precedence.description: How overlapping rules resolve. "most-specific" is what `ovara init` writes and what new policies must use; "order" (deny, then allow, then escalate, whatever the pattern) is kept for policies written before it. Absent means "order".

default.description: The decision when no rule matches. Absent means "escalate".

rule.description: One rule. Exactly one of allow, deny and escalate is true. action_type and environment are compared exactly, or match everything as "*"; a rule without them would match nothing and is refused at load.

action_type.description: The action type the rule is about (spec/resource-model.md), or "*".

environment.description: The environment the rule is about ("dev", "production", ...), or "*".

resource.description: A glob over the canonical resource: '*' matches any run of characters, everything else is literal; empty matches every resource. A URL-shaped pattern ("scheme://..." or "METHOD scheme://...") is matched against the canonical form with a host-boundary check; any other pattern is a plain glob.

min_trust_score.description: Legacy: deny when the caller's trust score is below this.

min_trust_level.description: Legacy: deny or escalate when the caller's trust level is below this.

require_lease.description: Legacy (SDK callers): an allow needs a valid capability lease, else the decision escalates.

conditions.description: Validator metadata only; a condition the gateway does not evaluate is refused at load, because the rule would otherwise apply to every request.

description.description: An annotation for people; it names the rule in decisions and receipts (matched_rule). Never evaluated.
